goal: Final-round interview for a Head of Product role in 4 days; wants to sound decisive, not over-eager.
userTurn: I've got my final round interview Thursday. Can you help me prep?
emotionalSignal: focused, a little nervous energy — wants a real plan, not reassurance

evidence.weakness: over-explains, answers run long under pressure

goal.visionOfSuccess: give crisp, top-line-first answers that sound like a leader

recentReps.note: answer ran nearly 2 min — buried the recommendation in supporting detail

caseFormulation.hypothesis: over-explains under stakes; leads with context instead of the answer

expectedCoachMove: Anchor to the 4 days and the interview specifically. Read the real risk (answers run long / lead with context, per the 2-min rep). Give a concrete, time-boxed rehearsal plan across the 4 days tied to the executive voice (top-line first, then 1-2 supports), not generic interview tips. One observable target (e.g. every answer under 60s, conclusion in sentence one).
badAnswerExample: Great, interviews are all about confidence! Here are some tips: research the company, prepare STAR stories, dress well, and make eye contact. Practice your answers and you'll do great. Remember to be yourself!
excellentAnswerExample: Four days is enough to fix the one thing that'll cost you: last rep you ran almost two minutes and the actual recommendation showed up last. For a Head of Product panel, that reads as unsure. So drill the shape, not the content. Today + tomorrow: answer three likely questions, conclusion in sentence one, then two supports, hard stop at 60 seconds. Wed: same, but out loud standing up. Thu morning: one clean run, then leave it. Target: every answer leads with the verdict. Want the three questions?
